name: Family Reunification / Family Formation

qualifying_event.description: The spouse or minor child of a qualifying sponsor may apply for a residence permit to join that sponsor in Aruba. Qualifying sponsors are: holders of non-compulsory status under LTUV (National Ordinance on Admission and Expulsion) article 1A or 1B; permanent residence permit holders; temporary residence permit holders with at least 3 years of legal residence; or temporarily admitted government/immigrant workers.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Marriage registry excerpt (DBSB); birth certificate or adoption proof for minors; original legal documentation for applicants 18 or older.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires being the spouse, or a minor child (or adopted/recognised child), of a qualifying sponsor in Aruba.

The sponsor must hold one of: non-compulsory LTUV article 1A/1B status; a permanent residence permit; a temporary residence permit held for at least 3 years; or temporarily-admitted government/immigrant worker status.

outcome.duration_length: tied to the sponsor's status; not specified in the source reviewed

sources.title: DIMAS, Government of Aruba -- Family Reunification: four qualifying sponsor-status categories, required documentation, explicit no-paid-work rule for family members joining under most sponsor categories

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Aruba's initial build. Distinct from aw_living_with_partner.json (a narrower, unmarried-partner-specific route requiring the Dutch sponsor to be born in Aruba) -- this route instead turns on the SPONSOR's immigration status (LTUV status holder, PR holder, 3-year+ temporary resident, or admitted government/immigrant worker) rather than the sponsor's nationality or place of birth, and explicitly covers married spouses and minor children. No sponsor income-threshold figure was found on this page (unlike aw_living_with_partner.json's explicit CBS-minimum-wage test) -- not invented here; flagged as a gap. work_rights is 'none' per the source's explicit statement that family members admitted under the permanent-residence-holder, temporary-residence-holder, and admitted-worker sponsor categories may not work -- the LTUV 1A/1B category's work-rights treatment was not separately specified and is conservatively modelled the same way pending clarification.
